scope: Read-only comparison of two hosted member-chat resource-invalid attempts; no source change, threshold change, or dispatch.

policy.interpretation: The acceptance samples exceeded both busy limits while one-minute load was above the high-load trigger. The guard's invalid decisions are supported by its measurements.

runs.terminal: The child exited 1 after the first CPU_PENDING sample; resource final invalid exit 3. No second WATCH_UNSAFE sample was recorded.
Watchdog requested stop at safe boundary, then resource final invalid exit 3 at 02:34:49.310Z.
runs.member_chat_result: not tested; no native report or Chat transport was uploaded

attribution.supported: CPU saturation arose during owned Chromium startup with concurrent host/OS activity. Both categories consumed measured CPU in the brief process brackets.
attribution.not_supported: The evidence cannot assign the full iostat busy interval to the extension, owned Chromium, the GitHub host, or a single macOS service; nor can it establish a member product failure.
attribution.measurement_limit: Before/after ps CPU-time snapshots bracket an approximately one-second iostat measurement interval; admission cpuSampleIntervalSeconds config controls spacing, not a ten-second iostat measurement. Exited/new/reparented/PID-reused processes cannot be assigned exactly. These snapshots do not continuously measure the entire time between guard polls.
attribution.missing_evidence_for_narrower_cause: Continuous synchronized per-process CPU attribution through browser startup, including short-lived host services, plus a resource-valid member result. Sparse one-second samples do not establish uninterrupted saturation between polls.

source_lifecycle_comparison.hosted_preflight: The package phase awaits npm install; the browser phase awaits Playwright's Chromium download and exits. The acceptance phase writes the member link to a private file, then spawns and awaits one native driver. These phases do not launch a reviewer-login browser before acceptance.
source_lifecycle_comparison.common_native_harness: Both guest and member use runNativeSidepanelQa. It creates one fresh owned profile and one Chrome child, then attaches Playwright to that child's verified CDP endpoint. Its finally awaits CDP detach, fixture server close, owned child exit, and profile removal.
source_lifecycle_comparison.member_login: The reviewer sign-in creates one new page in the already owned browser context inside exercisePanel, after common startup and panel readiness. Its finally awaits the page close. No second browser or profile is launched for reviewer login.
source_lifecycle_comparison.process_tree_at_first_568_cpu_spike: Raw member journal shows one owned Chromium root PID 5750, child of the native driver PID 5745, with Chromium Helpers under PID 5750. The interval bracket has no other Chromium root. This disproves a visible duplicate owned browser at that sample, but cannot inventory processes outside the sampled intervals.
source_lifecycle_comparison.verdict: No concrete retained preflight Chromium, duplicate profile, unawaited teardown, or avoidable member-only startup work was established. No source repair is supported by these runs.

successful_guest_startup_contrast.acceptance_admission: 2026-10-20T02:23:28.359Z; 3% busy on four logical CPUs; one-minute load 0.71
successful_guest_startup_contrast.recovery_samples: At 02:24:01 busy fell to 3%; at 02:24:17 it was 22%. The run continued and its acceptance resource final was valid at 02:26:55.371Z.
successful_guest_startup_contrast.interpretation: A single initial Chromium startup spike also occurred on a successful guest run. The persistent second unsafe sample, not the first spike alone, distinguishes the resource-invalid member 0.2.568 attempt. Separate hosted machines prevent attributing that difference to guest versus member product code.

existing_runner_choices.workflow_and_admission: The current hosted workflow and hosted-release-member-admission script allow only macos-15-intel (X64) or macos-15 (ARM64) for member-chat; both use the same unchanged resource guard.
existing_runner_choices.macos_15_arm_history: A prior 0.2.542 member-chat ARM64 attempt was resource-invalid at 94% busy on three logical CPUs, with Metal compiler and Chromium load; earlier member Settings ARM64 also stopped on high CPU. This is an allowed alternate architecture, not a demonstrated larger or quiescent capacity option.

decision: Stop repeating the same hosted member launch under the observed host conditions. Preserve normal resource thresholds and refusal. Resume only after an independently evidenced capacity change and a fresh normal admission; switching to the existing ARM label alone is not a proven capacity remedy.
